children: shares rose 2.1% in premarket trading Tuesday after the microcap explorer received environmental approval to begin exploration at the La Rosada prospect within its Laguna Salada uranium project in Argentina.

The Environmental Impact Assessment approval from the Ministry of Environment of Chubut Province covers six properties totaling about 59,895 hectares. That represents roughly 25% of Laguna Salada’s approximately 230,000-hectare exploration area and clears Jaguar to begin prospecting after the winter season.
For investors, the approval removes a regulatory hurdle and allows Jaguar

to start evaluating a large portion of Laguna Salada for potential uranium and vanadium deposits. However, La Rosada remains an early-stage exploration prospect, meaning the permit does not establish the size, grade or economic viability of any mineral resource. For a microcap explorer, results from the upcoming field program could therefore have an outsized effect on investor perceptions of the project’s value.

plans geological mapping, geochemical sampling and radiometric surveys across La Rosada. The company also intends to use electrical resistivity tomography to search for deeper ancient river channels that could contain mineralization.

La Rosada is about 45 kilometers northeast of Laguna Salada’s Guanaco prospect, which received its own environmental approval in March. The latest authorization expands the portion of the broader project where Jaguar can conduct exploration work.
The company didn't announce a drilling schedule or provide an estimate for when results from the La Rosada exploration program could become available.

title: Jaguar Uranium gains Argentina approval for La Rosada exploration
